Meta-analysis across cohorts for sc-ExWAS

Source: R/meta-analysis.R
run_meta_exwas.Rd

Combines independent-cohort sc-ExWAS estimates using inverse-variance weighted fixed-effect synthesis or random-effects synthesis. Keys are matched exactly on gene, cell type, and exposure.

Usage

run_meta_exwas(
  results_list,
  cohort_names = NULL,
  method = c("fixed", "random"),
  effect_col = NULL,
  se_col = NULL
)

Arguments

results_list

A list of DataFrames or data frames. Each cohort must contain unique gene-celltype-exposure keys and an effect estimate plus standard error.

cohort_names

Character vector with one unique name per cohort. Defaults to Cohort_1, Cohort_2, and so forth.

method

Character. "fixed" (default), or "random" for REML between-cohort variance with Hartung–Knapp inference. Random-effects synthesis requires metafor and at least three cohorts per key.

effect_col

Optional character scalar naming the effect column. When NULL, the first available column among log2FC, log2FoldChange, and estimate is used separately in each cohort.

se_col

Optional character scalar naming the standard-error column. When NULL, the first available column among se and lfcSE is used separately in each cohort. edgeR QL results from run_sc_exwas are deliberately unsupported because glmQLFTest does not supply coefficient standard errors.

Value

A DataFrame with one row per exact key and columns meta_effect, meta_se, meta_statistic, meta_df, meta_pvalue, meta_padj, I2, Q_pvalue, tau2, n_cohorts, cohorts, direction, and method. Under Hartung–Knapp inference meta_statistic is a t statistic with meta_df degrees of freedom; under fixed-effect synthesis it is a z statistic and meta_df is Inf.

Details

Fixed-effect synthesis uses $$\hat{\beta} = \frac{\sum_i w_i\hat{\beta}_i}{\sum_i w_i}, \quad w_i = 1/SE_i^2.$$ Random-effects synthesis uses restricted maximum likelihood for \(\tau^2\) and Hartung–Knapp small-sample inference. It is deliberately unavailable for only two cohorts. The \(I^2\) and Cochran Q statistics are reported as heterogeneity diagnostics; they do not establish transportability or independence of the contributing cohorts.

The function never maps gene identifiers or cell-type labels. Harmonisation must occur before calling it. Within-cohort duplicate keys are an error, preventing accidental double weighting after label aggregation. Inverse-variance synthesis also rejects edgeR QL results from run_sc_exwas, recognised by their method label or their metadata, because the QL F test supplies no coefficient standard errors. Use a backend that estimates valid coefficient standard errors for each independent cohort before meta-analysis.

References

Borenstein M et al. (2009). Introduction to Meta-Analysis. Wiley.

Viechtbauer W (2010). Conducting meta-analyses in R with the metafor package. Journal of Statistical Software 36:1–48. doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03

Examples

library(S4Vectors)
r1 <- DataFrame(
    gene = c("A", "B"), celltype = "Mono",
    log2FC = c(0.5, -0.3), se = c(0.1, 0.15),
    exposure = "PM2.5"
)
r2 <- DataFrame(
    gene = c("A", "B", "C"), celltype = "Mono",
    log2FC = c(0.4, -0.1, 0.2), se = c(0.12, 0.2, 0.1),
    exposure = "PM2.5"
)
meta <- run_meta_exwas(
    list(r1, r2),
    cohort_names = c("CohortA", "CohortB")
)
meta
#> DataFrame with 2 rows and 16 columns
#>          gene    celltype meta_effect   meta_se meta_statistic   meta_df
#>   <character> <character>   <numeric> <numeric>      <numeric> <numeric>
#> 1           A        Mono    0.459016 0.0768221        5.97505       Inf
#> 2           B        Mono   -0.228000 0.1200000       -1.90000       Inf
#>   meta_pvalue        I2  Q_pvalue      tau2 n_cohorts    exposure
#>     <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <integer> <character>
#> 1 2.30013e-09         0  0.522053         0         2       PM2.5
#> 2 5.74331e-02         0  0.423711         0         2       PM2.5
#>           cohorts   direction                 method   meta_padj
#>       <character> <character>            <character>   <numeric>
#> 1 CohortA;CohortB          ++ inverse_variance_fixed 4.60027e-09
#> 2 CohortA;CohortB          -- inverse_variance_fixed 5.74331e-02
